Label: Five Axis Machining
Description: A process where a workpiece is operated on using three linear axes and two rotational axes simultaneously for precise and complex machining.

Label: Seven Axis Machining
Description: A process that utilizes a machine tool with seven independent axes of movement to precisely cut material into specific dimensions and finishes.

Label: Abrasive Cleaning
Description: A process where contaminants are removed from a surface using abrasive materials under high pressure, without damaging the underlying structure.

Label: Abrasive Finishing
Description: A process that removes material from a workpiece surface using abrasive particles to enhance surface finish, dimensional accuracy, and mechanical properties.

Label: Abrasive Machining
Description: A process where material is removed from a workpiece by a multitude of small abrasive particles, typically through grinding, honing, or lapping.

Label: Additive Manufacturing
Description: The process that creates three-dimensional objects by building them layer by layer from a digital model.

Label: Adhesive Bonding
Description: A process that involves joining two surfaces together using a filler material, typically a polymer, to create a strong, durable bond.

Label: Age Quench Hardening
Description: A process where materials are heated, aged, and then rapidly cooled to increase hardness, strength, and resistance to wear and tear.

Label: Air Quench Hardening
Description: A process where heated metal parts are rapidly cooled in a controlled air environment to increase hardness and mechanical strength.

Label: Alkaline Oxide Conversion Coating
Description: A process where metal surfaces are treated with alkaline chemical solutions to form a protective, corrosion-resistant oxide conversion coating.

Label: Annealing
Description: A process where a material, typically metal or glass, is heated and then cooled slowly to reduce hardness and increase ductility.

Label: Anodizing
Description: A process where a protective oxide layer is electrochemically built on the surface of certain metals, primarily aluminum, to increase corrosion resistance.

Label: Atomic Hydrogen Welding
Description: A process where atomic hydrogen is used to generate high temperatures, facilitating the fusion of metals in a controlled environment.

Label: Austempering
Description: A process where steel or iron alloys are heat-treated at a constant temperature to improve hardness, strength, and toughness.

Label: Babbitting
Description: A process where a layer of Babbitt metal is applied to bearing surfaces to reduce friction and wear, enhancing performance and longevity.

Label: Bar Drawing
Description: A process where a metal bar is drawn through a die, reducing its diameter and increasing its length while improving surface finish and dimensional accuracy.

Label: Barrel Finishing
Description: A process where parts are smoothed or polished by tumbling in a barrel with abrasive materials, enhancing their surface finish and geometry.

Label: Bead Blasting
Description: A process where small glass, ceramic, or steel beads are propelled at high velocity to clean or finish a surface.

Label: Belt Sanding
Description: A process where abrasive belts are used to remove material from surfaces, improving finish and achieving precise dimensions.

Label: Bending
Description: A process where a machine applies force to a workpiece, causing it to deform along an axis, creating an angle in the material.

Label: Bevelling
Description: A process where edges of a material are cut at an angle to create a sloped surface, enhancing joint strength and aesthetic appeal.

Label: Black Oxide Coating
Description: A process where iron-based materials are treated with a hot alkaline solution to form a magnetite layer, enhancing corrosion resistance and reducing light reflection.

Label: Blanking
Description: A process where a punch and die cut flat material into precise, predetermined shapes, typically used for high-volume production of metal parts.

Label: Blow Molding
Description: A process where a heated plastic tube is inflated into a mold to form hollow parts, such as bottles or containers.

Label: Boring
Description: A process that involves enlarging a hole or tunnel using a cutting tool with a single-point cutting edge to improve concentricity.

Label: Braze Welding
Description: A process where a filler metal is heated above melting point and distributed between two or more close-fitting parts to join them without melting the base materials.

Label: Brazing
Description: A process where metals are joined by melting a filler material that has a lower melting point than the base materials.

Label: Broaching
Description: A process that involves removing material through a linear motion of a multi-tooth cutting tool called a broach, to produce precise finishes and dimensions.

Label: Buffing
Description: A process where a surface is polished to a high shine or smooth finish using a buffing wheel and abrasive compounds.

Label: Bulge Forming
Description: A process where internal pressure is applied to a tube within a die, causing the material to expand and conform to the die's shape.

Label: Butt Welding
Description: A process where two materials are joined end-to-end by applying heat and pressure, resulting in a continuous, single piece through coalescence and fusion.

Label: CNC Cylindrical Grinding
Description: A process where a computer numerically controlled (CNC) machine grinds the outer or inner diameter of a cylindrical part to precise dimensions and surface finish.

Label: CNC Laser Cutting
Description: A process that utilizes computer-controlled lasers to precisely cut or engrave materials, based on a pre-programmed design.

Label: CNC Machining
Description: A process that utilizes computer-controlled machine tools to remove material from a workpiece, following a pre-programmed path, to create precise parts.

Label: CNC Milling
Description: A process that involves the use of computer numerical control (CNC) to operate a milling machine for precise material removal.

Label: CNC Punching
Description: A process where computer-controlled punching machines create holes and shapes in sheet metal with high precision and repeatability.

Label: CNC Routing
Description: A process that utilizes computer numerical control (CNC) to direct a router or spindle to cut and shape materials such as wood, plastic, or metal.

Label: CNC Turning
Description: A process that involves a computer numerical control (CNC) machine rotating a workpiece while a cutting tool shapes the material.

Label: Cadmium Plating
Description: A process where a cadmium layer is electrochemically deposited onto a workpiece to provide corrosion resistance, lubricity, and galvanic compatibility.

Label: Carbide Machining
Description: A process where solid carbide, carbide-tipped, or carbide insert cutting tools are used to machine hard materials in precision manufacturing.

Label: Carbon Arc Welding
Description: A process where intense heat generated from a carbon arc is used to melt and fuse metal materials together for joining purposes.

Label: Carbon Dioxide Mold Casting
Description: A sand casting process where a mold is hardened by reacting carbon dioxide gas with a sodium silicate binder in the sand.

Label: Carbonitriding
Description: A process where a ferrous material is heated in a gaseous carbon-nitrogen environment to induce surface hardening through diffusion of carbon and nitrogen atoms.

Label: Carburizing
Description: A process where steel or iron surfaces are hardened by heating in a carbon-rich environment, allowing carbon absorption and diffusion into the material.

Label: Casting
Description: The process is where a liquid material, often molten metal poured or injected into a mold.

Label: Centerless Grinding
Description: A process where material removal is conducted through abrasive cutting, without a spindle or fixture, to achieve precision cylindrical surfaces.

Label: Centrifugal Casting
Description: A metal casting process that uses centrifugal force to distribute molten metal uniformly into a rotating mold, resulting in a defect-free part with excellent material integrity

Label: Ceramic Mold Casting
Description: A metal casting process that utilizes ceramic materials to create molds for precise and complex shapes, often used for tooling, dies, and high-temperature applications like aerospace components.

Label: Chemical Cleaning
Description: A process where contaminants on a material surface are removed using chemical or electrochemical solutions in a controlled manner.

Label: Chemical Coating
Description: A process where a substrate is covered with a layer of a chemical solution to enhance corrosion resistance, adhesion, and wear resistance.

Label: Chemical Conversion Coating
Description: A process where a metal surface is treated with a chemical solution to form a corrosion-resistant, protective outer layer.

Label: Chemical Engraving
Description: A process where controlled chemical corrosion is used to etch or engrave designs onto a metal surface.

Label: Chemical Etching
Description: A process where material is removed from a substrate using chemical reactions to create precise patterns or features on the surface.

Label: Chemical Machining
Description: A process where material removal occurs through controlled chemical erosion, typically by etching with acidic or alkaline solutions.

Label: Chemical Mechanical Polishing
Description: A process where a combination of chemical reactions and mechanical forces are used to smooth and planarize a material's surface.

Label: Chemical Polishing
Description: A process that utilizes chemical reactions to smooth and polish the surface of a metal, enhancing its appearance and corrosion resistance.

Label: Chemical Processing
Description: A process where raw materials undergo chemical reactions to transform into finished products, involving techniques like oxidation, reduction, and hydrolysis.

Label: Chemical Vapor Deposition
Description: A process where a solid material is deposited from a vapor by a chemical reaction occurring on or near a heated surface.

Label: Chromate Conversion Coating
Description: A process where a chromate solution is applied to a metal surface to form a protective, corrosion-resistant layer.

Label: Chrome Plating
Description: A process where a thin layer of chromium is electroplated onto a metal or plastic object to enhance durability, corrosion resistance, and aesthetic appeal.

Label: Chromizing
Description: A process that involves depositing a chromium layer onto a metal substrate to enhance its corrosion and wear resistance.

Label: Cladding
Description: a process can consistently produce outputs that meet predetermined specifications or requirements.

Label: Clinching
Description: A process where sheet metal parts are joined by plastically deforming and interlocking material without using additional components or heat.

Label: Coating
Description: A process where a substrate is covered with a layer of material to improve surface properties such as appearance, adhesion, wetability, corrosion resistance, or wear resistance.

Label: Coining
Description: Coining is a precision closed-die forging process where a workpiece is compressed between two dies under very high pressure to create fine detailed features, smooth surfaces, and tight dimensional tolerances.

Label: Cold Chamber Die Casting
Description: A manufacturing process where molten metal, often aluminum or magnesium, is heated in a separate furnace and then transferred to the die casting machine.

Label: Cold Drawing
Description: A process where metal is pulled through a die to reduce its diameter, improve surface finish, and enhance mechanical properties without heating.

Label: Cold Extrusion
Description: A process where metal billets are forced through a die at room temperature, enhancing mechanical properties and dimensional accuracy without thermal degradation.

Label: Cold Forging
Description: A process where metal is plastically deformed at room temperature using compressive forces to increase strength and achieve precise dimensional tolerances.

Label: Cold Forming
Description: A process where metal is plastically deformed at room temperature to increase strength, improve surface finish, and achieve precise dimensional tolerances.

Label: Cold Isostatics Pressing
Description: A process where powdered materials are compacted into dense, uniform shapes using high-pressure fluid applied isotropically at ambient temperature.

Label: Cold Rolling
Description: A process where metal is passed through rollers below recrystallization temperature, increasing strength and hardness while reducing thickness and improving surface finish.

Label: Cold Treatment
Description: A process where materials are subjected to low temperatures to improve hardness, strength, and stress relief without altering their original structure.

Label: Cold Vacuum Pressing
Description: A process where materials are compressed at low temperatures in a vacuum environment to eliminate air pockets and enhance bonding strength.

Label: Cold Working
Description: A process where metal is plastically deformed below its recrystallization temperature, enhancing strength and hardness through strain hardening without altering its phase.

Label: Combustible Gas Welding
Description: A process where a combustible gas, typically acetylene, is used to generate heat, melting the workpieces to form a joint.

Label: Compression Molding
Description: A process where thermosetting plastics are preheated, placed in a mold, and subjected to pressure to form complex, high-strength parts.

Label: Continuous Casting
Description: A process where molten metal is solidified into a continuous length, usually in the form of slabs, billets, or blooms.

Label: Contour Machining
Description: A process where CNC machine tools cut along curved or angled paths to produce complex contoured shapes with high accuracy.

Label: Contour Milling
Description: A process where milling machines cut along curved or angled paths to create contoured or complex 3D surfaces with precision.

Label: Copper Plating
Description: A process where a workpiece is coated with a thin layer of copper by electrochemical deposition from a copper ion solution.

Label: Coremaking
Description: A process where sand cores are created using binders and heat to form internal cavities and passages in metal castings.

Label: Corrugation
Description: A process where flat sheets of material are mechanically formed into a series of parallel ridges and grooves to enhance structural rigidity.

Label: Counter Boring
Description: A process where a larger diameter hole is drilled into an existing hole to create a stepped hole or to accommodate a fastener head.

Label: Counter Sinking
Description: A process that involves enlarging and beveling the top of a drilled hole to allow a flat-headed fastener to sit flush with a surface.

Label: Creep Feed Grinding
Description: A process where high-precision abrasive machining is performed with a slow, deep-cutting grinding action on hard materials using a specialized machine.

Label: Crochet
Description: A process that involves creating fabric by interlocking loops of yarn, thread, or strands of other materials using a crochet hook.

Label: Curing
Description: A process where polymers, composites, adhesives, or coatings are hardened through chemical reactions or thermal treatment.

Label: Curvic Grinding
Description: A process where precise, curved, tooth-like forms are ground into surfaces to enable high torque transmissions and accurate alignment in mechanical systems.

Label: Custom Tubing
Description: A process that involves fabricating tubes to specific dimensions and material specifications as per individual customer requirements.

Label: Cut to Length Tubing
Description: A process where specific lengths of tubing are produced by cutting longer tubes using precise, automated machinery.

Label: Cyaniding
Description: A process where steel parts are heated in a cyanide bath to create a hard, wear-resistant surface through the formation of a thin layer of iron cyanide.

Label: Cylindrical Grinding
Description: A process where an abrasive wheel removes material from a workpiece's external surface to achieve precise diameter and surface finish.

Label: Cylindrical Silk Screen Printing
Description: A process where screen printing techniques are applied to cylindrical or curved surfaces such as bottles, tubes, or containers.

Label: Deburring
Description: A process where residual material edges or protrusions are removed from a workpiece after machining operations, enhancing its quality and safety.

Label: Decorative Anodizing
Description: A process where aluminum surfaces are electrolytically treated to form a durable, corrosion-resistant, and aesthetic oxide layer.

Label: Deep Drawing
Description: A process where a metal blank is radially drawn into a forming die by a mechanical punch, creating a hollow, cup-like structure.

Label: Deep Hole Drilling
Description: A process that involves creating deep, straight holes in a material using specialized drilling machines and tools for precision and accuracy.

Label: Diamond Machining
Description: A process where ultra-precision cutting tools with diamond tips are used to machine materials with high surface quality and dimensional accuracy.

Label: Die Casting
Description: A process where molten metal is forced under high pressure into a specialized metal mold (die).

Label: Die Forging
Description: A process where metal is plastically deformed under high pressure using dies to produce components with improved mechanical properties and dimensional accuracy.

Label: Die Making
Description: A process where precision tools and dies are designed and fabricated to shape, cut, or form materials in manufacturing operations.

Label: Die Sinking
Description: A process where an electrically conductive workpiece is shaped by controlled erosion using a spark discharge between the workpiece and a shaped electrode.

Label: Diffusion Bonding
Description: A process where materials are joined through atomic diffusion at elevated temperature and pressure, without melting, resulting in a monolithic structure.

Label: Diffusion Hardening
Description: A process where carbon or nitrogen atoms are diffused into a metal surface to increase hardness, wear resistance, and fatigue strength.

Label: Dip Brazing
Description: A process where components are joined by immersing them in a molten filler metal, which then cools to form a strong, sealed joint.

Label: Dip Soldering
Description: A process where electronic components are submerged into molten solder to create reliable, conductive joints between the component and the circuit board.

Label: Direct Extrusion
Description: A process where a billet is heated and forced through a die, reducing cross-sectional area and increasing length, to produce a desired profile.

Label: Directed Energy Deposition
Description: A process where focused thermal energy fuses material, typically metal powder or wire, layer by layer to build or repair components.

Label: Drawing
Description: A process where metal is pulled through a die to reduce its cross-section and increase its length, commonly used in wire and tube production.

Label: Drilling
Description: A process where a rotating cutting tool, known as a drill bit, is used to cut a hole of circular cross-section in solid materials.

Label: Drop Forging
Description: A process where heated metal is shaped by being placed between two dies and hammered, enhancing strength and structural integrity.

Label: Drop On Demand
Description: The process where ink droplets are ejected only when needed to print a specific dot on a surface.

Label: Drying
Description: A process where moisture or solvents are removed from materials, coatings, or products using heat, air, vacuum, or other methods.

Label: Dyeing
Description: A process where textiles are treated with a soluble colorant to impart a permanent and resistant color.

Label: ECG Tube Cutting
Description: A process where electrical discharge machining is utilized to cut precise shapes into electro-conductive materials, specifically tubes.

Label: EDM
Description: A process that utilizes electrical discharges to remove material from a workpiece, known as Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM).

Label: Electric Arc Welding
Description: A process where an electric arc between an electrode and the workpiece generates heat to melt and join metals.

Label: Electrical Resistance Welding
Description: A process where heat generated from electrical resistance is used to join or fuse metal parts together under applied pressure.

Label: Electro Chemical Machining
Description: A process where material is removed from a workpiece through anodic dissolution using a controlled electrolyte flow and electrical current.

Label: Electro Deposition
Description: A process where metal ions in a solution are reduced and deposited onto a conductive substrate via an electric current.

Label: Electro Forming
Description: A process where metal is deposited onto a mandrel through electroplating, creating precise, intricate components after mandrel removal.

Label: Electroplating
Description: A process where a metal workpiece is coated with a thin layer of another metal via electrodeposition to enhance corrosion resistance, wearability, or aesthetics.

Label: Electro Slag Welding
Description: A process where high current is passed through a consumable electrode to melt and weld thick metal plates using slag's heat conductivity.

Label: Electrochemical Grinding
Description: A process where material removal is achieved by combined mechanical grinding and electrochemical erosion, reducing stress and thermal damage.

Label: Electrochemical Processes
Description: A process where electrical energy drives chemical reactions to deposit, dissolve, or alter materials on a workpiece at the atomic level.

Label: Electrocoating
Description: A process where electrically charged particles deposit onto a conductive substrate, forming a uniform, corrosion-resistant coating through electrodeposition.

Label: Electrodeposited Coating
Description: A process where metal ions are deposited onto a substrate via electrolysis, forming a uniform, adherent coating for enhanced surface properties.

Label: Electroless Nickel Plating
Description: A process where a nickel-phosphorus alloy is deposited onto a metal surface via chemical reduction, enhancing corrosion resistance and hardness.

Label: Electron Beam Machining
Description: A process where high-velocity electrons concentrated into a narrow beam are used to remove or cut material by melting or vaporizing it.

Label: Electron Beam Welding
Description: A process where high-velocity electrons are used to generate heat, causing fusion and joining materials, known as Electron Beam Welding.

Label: Electropolishing
Description: A process where metal surfaces are polished and smoothed by anodic dissolution in a concentrated electrolyte solution to reduce surface roughness.

Label: Embossing
Description: A process where a pattern is created on a material's surface by applying pressure, resulting in a raised or indented design.

Label: End Milling
Description: A process that involves rotating a multi-tooth cutter to remove material from a workpiece along its axis, creating precise profiles and slots.

Label: Engraving
Description: A process where material is incised or carved to create designs, typically utilizing tools or lasers for precision and detail.

Label: Erosion Machining
Description: A process where material is removed from a workpiece through controlled surface erosion using high-velocity fluid, typically water or oil.

Label: Etching
Description: A process that utilizes chemical or plasma reactive ion techniques to remove material from a substrate, creating precise patterns in microfabrication.

Label: Explosion Forming
Description: A process where a controlled explosive charge deforms metal sheets into complex shapes by generating high-pressure shock waves in a containment chamber.

Label: Explosive Welding
Description: A process where high-velocity explosives are used to bond two dissimilar metals together, creating a high-quality weld without heat or deformation.

Label: Extruding
Description: A process that involves forcing material through a die to create objects with a fixed cross-sectional profile.

Label: Extrusion Blow Molding
Description: A process where a heated plastic tube is inflated into a mold to form hollow objects, utilizing high pressure air in extrusion blow molding.

Label: Fabricating
Description: A process that involves cutting, shaping, and assembling components to create finished products from raw or semi-finished materials.

Label: Face Milling
Description: A process where a rotating cutter with multiple cutting edges removes material from a workpiece to create a flat surface perpendicular to the tool axis.

Label: Facing
Description: A process where a cutting tool machines the end of a rotating workpiece to create a flat surface, typically performed on a lathe.

Label: Filament Winding
Description: A process where continuous fibers are wound under tension onto a rotating mandrel to create composite structures with high strength-to-weight ratios.

Label: Fine Blanking
Description: A process that produces precise, smooth-edged components by shearing material between a punch and die with high pressure and minimal clearance.

Label: Flame Hardening
Description: A process where heat from a high-temperature flame is applied to a metal surface, followed by rapid cooling, to increase its hardness and wear resistance.

Label: Flame Spraying
Description: A process where a heat source melts a coating material, which is then sprayed onto a surface to form a protective or decorative layer.

Label: Flanging EDM
Description: A process where controlled electrical discharges remove material from a workpiece, creating precise flanges via erosion in Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM).

Label: Flat Rolling
Description: A process where metal slabs are compressed between rotaxting rolls to reduce thickness and achieve uniform cross-sectional dimensions.

Label: Flow Drilling
Description: A process where a rotating conical tool generates frictional heat to form holes and bushings in thin-walled materials without producing chips.

Label: Flow Forming
Description: A process where a rotating metal blank is axially compressed and elongated by rollers to form precise cylindrical components with enhanced mechanical properties.

Label: Flux-Cored Arc Welding
Description: A process where a continuous tubular wire filled with flux is used to create an electric arc, resulting in a weld.

Label: Forging
Description: A process where metal is heated and deformed under high pressure to produce stronger, more durable parts with improved microstructure.

Label: Forming
Description: A process where materials are deformed or reshaped without adding or removing material, typically involving bending, stretching, or compressing.

Label: Friction Drilling
Description: A process where a rotating conical tool generates heat through friction to penetrate and form holes in metal without producing chips.

Label: Friction Welding
Description: A process where heat generated from mechanical friction between workpieces, combined with a force to press them together, creates a solid-state weld.

Label: Full Annealing
Description: A process where a metal is heated to a specific temperature, held, then cooled slowly to relieve internal stresses and improve ductility and toughness.

Label: Furnace Brazing
Description: A process where metals are joined by melting a filler metal between work pieces in a controlled atmosphere furnace, creating a strong, high-temperature resistant bond.

Label: Fused Deposition Modeling
Description: The process where a thermoplastic filament is melted and extruded through a nozzle to build objects layer by layer.

Label: Fused Filament Fabrication
Description: A process where thermoplastic filament is extruded layer-by-layer through a heated nozzle to create three-dimensional objects based on digital models.

Label: Fusion Joining
Description: A process where materials are joined by melting interfaces, allowing them to cool and solidify, forming a continuous bond without additional adhesives.

Label: Fusion Welding
Description: A process where materials are joined by melting interfaces, forming a joint upon solidification, often utilizing heat from an electric arc or laser.

Label: Galvanizing
Description: A process where a protective zinc coating is applied to steel or iron to prevent rusting and corrosion.

Label: Gas Brazing
Description: A process where filler metal is heated above melting point and distributed between two or more close-fitting parts by capillary action to join them.

Label: Gas Metal Arc Welding
Description: A process where an electric arc forms between a consumable wire electrode and the workpiece metal, heating both to create a weld pool.

Label: Gas Tungsten Arc Welding
Description: A process where an electric arc is formed between a tungsten electrode and the workpiece to create a weld using inert gas as a shield.

Label: Gas Welding
Description: A process where heat from a gas flame, typically oxy-acetylene, is used to melt interface surfaces, creating a joint upon cooling.

Label: Gear Cutting
Description: A process that involves the use of specialized tools to create precise, interlocking teeth on a gear wheel for mechanical transmission systems.

Label: Gear Gashing
Description: A process where large, rapid material removal from a gear blank is performed using a multi-tooth cutting tool, known as a gash cutter.

Label: Gear Hobbing
Description: A process where a specialized hobbing machine cuts teeth into a blank gear, utilizing continuous, synchronized rotations between the gear and the cutting tool.

Label: Gold Plating
Description: A process where a thin layer of gold is electrochemically deposited onto a substrate for enhanced conductivity, corrosion resistance, and aesthetic appeal.

Label: Gravity Casting
Description: A process where molten metal is poured into a mold and uses gravity to fill the cavities, solidifying into the final product.

Label: Grinding
Description: A process where material is reduced to a fine powder or sharp edges are smoothed through friction and abrasion, typically using a grinding wheel or machine.

Label: Grit Blasting
Description: A process where high-pressure air blasts small particles against a surface to remove contaminants, roughen, or smooth it for subsequent operations.

Label: Gun Drilling
Description: A process where deep, straight holes are drilled into a material using a high-speed, high-feed rate, single-flute drill bit.

Label: Hardening
Description: A process that involves heating a material, typically metal, to a specific temperature and then cooling it rapidly to increase its hardness and strength.

Label: Harperizing
Description: A process where metal parts are polished and deburred by tumbling in a mixture of ceramic media and water under high gravitational forces.

Label: Heading
Description: A process where metal is plastically deformed using dies and punches to form heads on fasteners like bolts and screws.

Label: Heat Sealing
Description: A process where heat and pressure are applied to thermoplastic materials to create a bond, forming a sealed joint between surfaces.

Label: Heat Treating
Description: A process where metals are heated and cooled under controlled conditions to alter their physical and mechanical properties, without changing the product shape.

Label: Hemming
Description: A process where sheet metal edges are folded over onto themselves to enhance strength, eliminate sharp edges, and improve aesthetic appearance.

Label: High Energy Beam Machining
Description: A process where focused high-energy beams, such as lasers or electron beams, are used to cut or drill materials with precision.

Label: High Energy Beam Welding
Description: A process where high-energy beams, such as lasers or electron beams, are used to melt and fuse materials together, creating a weld.

Label: High Speed Metal Cutting
Description: A process where metals are machined at very high cutting speeds to improve productivity, surface finish, and dimensional accuracy.

Label: Hobbing
Description: A process where a rotating hob cuts teeth into a workpiece, typically for gears or splines, using synchronized rotational movements.

Label: Hole Drilling EDM
Description: A process that utilizes electrical discharges to create precise holes in a workpiece using a rotating conductive tube as an electrode.

Label: Hole Making
Description: A process where specific tools, such as drills or punches, are used to create precise holes in a workpiece for assembly or operational purposes.

Label: Honing
Description: A process where abrasive stones are used to refine surface finish and geometry of a workpiece, typically in bore or cylinder applications.

Label: Horizontal Boring
Description: A process where a horizontal boring machine drills holes into workpieces, typically large, heavy materials, with precision and accuracy.

Label: Horizontal Milling
Description: A process where a horizontally oriented spindle performs multi-axis machining on a workpiece using a rotary cutter.

Label: Hot Chamber Die Casting
Description: A metal casting process where the injection system is submerged in a furnace containing molten metal.

Label: Hot Extrusion
Description: A process where heated material is forced through a die to produce continuous cross-sectional profiles, enhancing ductility and reducing required forming force.

Label: Hot Forming
Description: A process where metal is heated above recrystallization temperature and deformed to enhance ductility and reduce work hardening for complex geometries.

Label: Hot Isostatic
Description: A process where materials are subjected to high temperature and isostatic gas pressure to eliminate porosity and improve mechanical properties.

Label: Hot Rolling
Description: A process where metal is heated above recrystallization temperature and passed through rollers to reduce thickness and alter mechanical properties.

Label: Hot Spinning
Description: A process where a heated metal blank is rotated and formed over a mandrel using a roller to produce axisymmetric components.

Label: Hot Stamping
Description: A process where heated dies press metallic foils onto substrates, creating permanent designs through pressure and temperature-induced adhesion.

Label: Hot Vacuum Pressing
Description: A process where materials are heated and compressed in a vacuum environment to reduce porosity and increase density, enhancing mechanical properties.

Label: Hot Working
Description: A process where metals are plastically deformed above their recrystallization temperature, enhancing ductility and reducing work hardening for improved mechanical properties.

Label: Hydroforming
Description: A process where high-pressure hydraulic fluid shapes ductile metals into complex geometries within a die, enhancing structural integrity and material efficiency.

Label: Hypodermic Tubing
Description: A process where stainless steel is drawn into thin-walled tubes, typically for use in medical or industrial applications.

Label: ID-OD Grinding
Description: A process where internal and external diameters of a workpiece are ground to precise dimensions using a rotating grinding wheel.

Label: Impact Extrusion
Description: A process where a metal slug is forced into a die at high speed and pressure to create hollow or shaped parts, often from aluminum or soft metals.

Label: Impression Die Forging
Description: A process where metal is heated and pressed into a die to produce high-precision parts with excellent surface finish and dimensional accuracy.

Label: Indirect Extrusion
Description: A process where the billet remains stationary while the die assembly moves to create a product with a hollow or solid cross-section.

Label: Induction Brazing
Description: A process where electromagnetic fields heat metal pieces, allowing a filler metal to melt and create a joint, is called Induction Brazing.

Label: Induction Hardening
Description: A process that utilizes induction heating to harden a metal surface, increasing its resistance to wear and extending its lifespan.

Label: Induction Heading
Description: A process where electrically conductive materials are heated through electromagnetic induction, generating eddy currents and resistive heating for precise thermal applications.

Label: Induction Soldering
Description: A process where electromagnetic fields generate heat to melt solder, facilitating the joining of metal parts without direct contact.

Label: Infrared Brazing
Description: A process where infrared radiation is used to heat and join two metal pieces together using a filler metal, without melting the base materials.

Label: Infrared Soldering
Description: A process that utilizes infrared radiation to generate heat for melting and flowing solder, facilitating the joining of metal surfaces in electronic assemblies.

Label: Injection Blow Molding
Description: A process where molten plastic is injected into a mold to form a preform, then inflated to create hollow products like bottles.

Label: Injection Molding
Description: A process where molten material is injected into a mold to produce parts with complex geometries in high volumes.

Label: Investment Casting
Description: A process where a wax pattern is coated in ceramic material, hardened, then heated to remove wax, creating a mold for molten metal casting.

Label: Iridite
Description: A process where aluminum surfaces are coated with a protective chromate conversion layer, enhancing corrosion resistance and electrical conductivity.

Label: Iron Soldering
Description: A process where a filler metal is heated to join iron pieces together, creating a strong, permanent bond through the application of intense heat.

Label: Ironing
Description: A process where sheet metal is thinned and elongated by passing through a series of dies, enhancing surface finish and dimensional accuracy.

Label: Isostatic Pressing
Description: A process where materials are compacted uniformly using high-pressure fluid in all directions to enhance density and mechanical properties.

Label: Jig Boring
Description: a precision machining process where a specialized machine tool, called a jig borer, is used to accurately enlarge and finish holes to extremely tight tolerances, often for locating dowels or alignment pins in tooling and dies.

Label: Joining

Description: A process that involves heating a steel part above its critical temperature, then rapidly cooling it, to increase hardness throughout the entire piece.

Label: Tin Plating
Description: A process where a thin layer of tin is electrochemically deposited onto a metal substrate to enhance corrosion resistance, solderability, and aesthetic appeal.

Label: Tool Making
Description: A process that involves designing, creating, and maintaining specialized tools used in manufacturing and production operations.

Label: Torch Brazing
Description: A process where a torch is used to melt filler metal, creating a joint between two base materials without melting them.

Label: Torch Cutting
Description: A process where a high-temperature flame, typically from an oxy-fuel torch, is used to sever, trim, or pierce metal materials.

Label: Torch Soldering
Description: A process where a torch generates heat to melt solder, creating a joint between two metal surfaces, typically in electronics or plumbing.

Label: Transfer Molding
Description: A process where pre-measured material is heated and pressurized into a mold cavity, solidifying to form a part upon cooling.

Label: Transfer Press Stamping
Description: An efficient manufacturing process used to craft medium to high volumes of metal components

Label: Trepanning
Description: A process where a rotating hollow cutter removes a core from a workpiece, creating large-diameter holes with minimal material waste.

Label: Tube Bending
Description: A process that involves deforming metal tubes into specific angles and radii using dedicated machinery and tooling.

Label: Tube Drawing
Description: A process where a tube is reduced in diameter and/or wall thickness by pulling it through a die, enhancing its mechanical properties.

Label: Tubing
Description: Tubing is a manufacturing operation used to create hollow cylindrical structures (tubes) with controlled dimensions and mechanical properties, typically from metal, plastic, or composite materials.

Label: Tufting
Description: A process where yarns are inserted into a backing material using needles to create pile surfaces, commonly employed in carpet and textile production.

Label: Tumble Finishing
Description: A process where parts are placed in a rotating barrel with abrasive media to deburr, polish, or clean surfaces through friction and impact.

Label: Tumbling
Description: A process that involves smoothing and polishing a rough surface by continuously turning it in a machine filled with abrasive substances.

Label: Turning
Description: A process that involves rotating a workpiece while a single-point cutting tool removes material, resulting in a cylindrical shape.

Label: Ultrasonic Cleaning
Description: A process where high-frequency sound waves create cavitation bubbles in a liquid to remove contaminants from solid surfaces.

Label: Ultrasonic Machining
Description: A process where high-frequency ultrasonic vibrations are applied to a tool, removing material from a workpiece through abrasive slurry, enabling precise machining.

Label: Ultrasonic Soldering
Description: A process that utilizes ultrasonic vibrations to create a reliable, flux-free metallurgical bond between dissimilar materials in soldering operations.

Label: Ultrasonic Welding
Description: A process that utilizes high-frequency ultrasonic acoustic vibrations to create solid-state welds between materials, typically plastics or lightweight metals.

Label: Unconventional Machining
Description: A process where material removal occurs through non-traditional methods such as electrical, chemical, or thermal energy, without direct mechanical contact.

Label: Upset Forging
Description: A process where metal is heated and compressed under high pressure at one end to increase its diameter, known as upset forging.

Label: Upsetting
Description: A process where metal is compressed axially to increase its diameter, enhancing mechanical properties and forming components like bolts and fasteners.

Label: Vacuum Assisted Resin Transfer Molding
Description: A process where resin is drawn into a sealed mold containing a dry fiber preform using vacuum pressure, ensuring complete saturation and void-free laminates.

Label: Vacuum Brazing
Description: A process where metals are joined at high temperatures in a vacuum environment to prevent oxidation and maintain material properties.

Label: Vacuum Casting
Description: A process where a vacuum is used to draw liquid material into a mold, ensuring precise replication of the mold's shape and details.

Label: Vacuum Forming
Description: A process where a heated thermoplastic sheet is shaped over a mold by applying vacuum pressure, creating detailed, uniform components.

Label: Vacuum Hardening
Description: A process where materials are heated in a vacuum environment and rapidly cooled to increase hardness and mechanical strength.

Label: Vacuum Molding
Description: A process where a sheet of plastic is heated to a forming temperature, stretched onto a single-surface mold, and forced against the mold by a vacuum.

Label: Vacuum Packaging
Description: A process where products are enclosed in airtight packaging under vacuum conditions to prevent oxidation, spoilage, and extend shelf life.

Label: Vacuum Pressing
Description: A process where materials are compressed and bonded under vacuum pressure, typically using heat and adhesive to form laminated or veneered products.

Label: Vacuum Thermoforming
Description: A process where a plastic sheet is heated to a pliable forming temperature, then shaped by a mold under vacuum pressure.

Label: Vapor Deposition
Description: A process where material is deposited onto a substrate in vapor form, forming a thin film through chemical or physical reactions.

Label: Vaporized Metal Coating
Description: A process where a metal is vaporized and condensed onto a substrate, forming a thin, uniform coating for enhanced surface properties.

Label: Vertical Boring
Description: A process where a rotating tool bores holes in a workpiece vertically, utilizing a vertical lathe or vertical boring mill.

Label: Vertical Milling
Description: A process where a rotating cutting tool removes material from a workpiece in a vertically oriented spindle in a milling machine.

Label: Vibratory Deburring
Description: A process where high-frequency vibrations are used to remove burrs and imperfections from manufactured metal parts.

Label: Vibratory Finishing
Description: A process where parts are deburred, polished, or cleaned by vibrating them with abrasive media in a specially designed container.

Label: Vibratory Tumbling
Description: A process where parts are polished or deburred by placing them in a vibrating container with abrasive media, facilitating surface refinement.

Label: Water Quench Hardening
Description: A process where heated metal parts are rapidly cooled in water, increasing hardness and strength through the formation of martensite.

Label: Waterjet Cutting
Description: A process where high-pressure water, often mixed with abrasives, is used to cut through materials with precision and without heat-induced distortion.

Label: Wave Soldering
Description: A process where electronic components are soldered onto a PCB using a molten solder wave, ensuring efficient and uniform connections.

Label: Weaving
Description: A process that interlaces two sets of yarns at right angles to generate a fabric or textile, typically executed on a loom.

Label: Wet Painting
Description: A process where a liquid paint is applied to a surface and cured, providing a protective or decorative layer on the manufactured product.

Label: Wire Bending
Description: A process where a machine or tool precisely deforms a wire into specific geometric configurations based on predefined specifications.

Label: Wire Drawing
Description: A process where a metal wire is reduced in diameter by pulling it through a series of dies under tension.

Label: Wire EDM
Description: A process that utilizes electrical discharges to cut intricate shapes or profiles into hard conductive materials with high precision.

Label: Wire Forming
Description: A process where metal wire or strip is bent, cut, and shaped using specialized machinery to produce components with precise geometries and dimensions.

Label: Wire Harness Assembly
Description: A process where individual wires, cables, and subassemblies are arranged, bound together, and fitted with connectors to form a wire harness.

Label: Wood Working
Description: A process that involves cutting, shaping, and assembling wood to construct products such as furniture, cabinetry, and sculptures.

Label: Zero Stock Machining
Description: A process where parts are produced on-demand, directly from raw materials, eliminating the need for inventory storage.

Label: Zinc Plating
Description: A process where a layer of zinc is electrochemically applied to a metal surface to provide corrosion resistance and enhance aesthetic appeal.

Label: Binder Jetting
Description: A process where a liquid binding agent selectively deposits onto a powder bed, layer by layer, to create solid parts from powdered materials.
